items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: So yeah, we did an album of his tunes.

ctx.x: And Fred Astaire? Is that the music that Fred Astaire was associated with?

Yeah, I mean composers seemed to love Fred Astaire for some reason. I mean he might not be a singer, it’s not a singer’s voice per se, it’s not like Crosby, Sinatra, Perry Como has got a very good voice and everything like that, and Tony Bennett up to a point, but I mean Fred Astaire had a way, I think because he had such a great rhythmic sense, being a dancer, his delivery was very light. And he sang those Berlin songs, you know like “Putting All My Eggs In One Basket.” [scats] He had a jazz feel in his singing,…
I see you were in on a Condon memorial thing too? Eddie Condon?
